successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: the Tuul valley, the upper Kherlen and the upper Onon, with the palace at present-day Ulan Bator, without the Merkit basins of the Selenga and lower Orkhon

ledger.x: c. 1000: the Keraites enter the Church of the East. 'They were absorbed into the Church of the East around 1000 by Metropolitan Abdisho' and 'converted... early in the 11th century'; the infobox starts the Keraites in the 11th century; the page's predecessors are the Zubu and the Kara-Khanid Khanate.

wars.name: Temüjin-Keraite war (Battle of the Burning Sands)
wars.outcome: Temüjin defeated the Keraites in 1203, the Toghrul page's Battle of the Burning Sands; Toghrul was killed among the Naimans; the Keraites merged with the Mongol Empire.

wars.name: Kerait-Mongol campaign against the Naimans
wars.outcome: 'In 1199, Temüjin together with an ally Ong khan launched a campaign against the Naimans' (Naimans page, read in the naiman dossier); the Toghrul page: 'Around 1199, Toghrul wanted to finish once and for all with the Naimans.'

certainty.note: A steppe khanate known from a few river names; no border on any page.
